column2: The location scan code must be unique.
The equipment scan code must be unique.
Reissuing the code KILLS every label already stuck on this equipment — they have to be reprinted and refitted.
The code has to start with "L" (a location label) or "A" (an equipment label). Received: %s
A scan code has to start with "L" (a location label) or "A" (an equipment label). Received: %s
The scan code has been reissued. Old labels out in the field no longer open anything — they have to be reprinted and refitted.
An EQUIPMENT label (a code starting with A): stuck on the\n                    equipment itself and travelling with it. Different from a\n                    location label.
This is the label of location %(ma)s — %(ten)s. No equipment is installed there today, so no equipment record can be opened.
No location carries the code "%s". The label may have been reissued — do not record readings against another record; tell the asset manager.
Reissuing the code KILLS every label out in the field for this location — they have to be reprinted and refitted. Only do it when a label has been copied or stuck in the wrong place.
The code printed on the QR label out in the field. Random, with a prefix by type — not a sequence number, so that nobody can work out how much equipment the plant has.
A LOCATION label (a code starting with L): scanning it gives\n the equipment installed here today. Replacing the\n equipment needs no new label.
No %(loai)s carries the code "%(ma)s". The label may have been reissued, or the record deleted. Do not record readings against another record — tell the asset manager to print a new label.
An equipment label: stuck on the equipment itself and travelling with it. Different from a location label, which is fixed to the tower and goes nowhere.
A location label: scanning it gives the equipment installed here today, looked up through the installation history. Replacing the equipment needs no new label.
